name: rice paddy ground tile (inaka-paddy-water)
label: jp_inaka_pack/gnd/inaka-paddy-water
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: paddy water ground tile (full 16x16 tiled texture of water with green plant tufts)

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain tile that fills the whole 16x16 area (width 16 on every row). It has no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no standing volume, only a repeating pattern of teal water cells with green and yellow-green tufts. The column scans show alternating light and dark runs with no top band followed by a front face. It is a flat ground texture, so it is not a standing object and the view-contract rows do not apply.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single small tile with only 7 distinct colours in total. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile, so the candidate is far below it. It only matches the paving reference's 7 per tile, and paving is a deliberately limited, regular pattern. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted teal and not a black sticker line. There are no 5x5 flat fills, and the dotted ripple texture is real but sparse. Shading is about 4 effective steps against the 5-6 Beodeul uses per material, and the surface lacks the multi-tone clumping and grain of the grass reference. Water can be simpler than grass, but this is thin next to the richer reference, and the piece also reads as one tile rather than a 4x3 patch. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: paddy water terrain tile (full 16x16 fill, flat tiling texture)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 16x16 opaque square (width 16 on every row) filled with teal/green water pixels and scattered lighter green/yellow plant specks, with a faint grid pattern. There is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no front face. It is a flat, seamless terrain fill, not a standing object, so the top/front structure rules do not apply. It matches the stated kind of terrain tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a speckled teal-green water patch with only 7 distinct colours in total, so about 4 usable lightness steps once the speckle accents are set aside. The grass reference has 80 colours and 26 per tile, and its clumps are shaded in 5-6 greens. The candidate has no 5x5 flat fills (0%), and the speckle breaks up the surface, so it is not flat. However, the pattern reads as a uniform noise or dither with no larger forms such as ripple clumps, reflections, mud edges or rice-shoot tufts. The paving reference also has 7 colours, but it gets its richness from stones shaded one by one and a clear structure, and the candidate has neither. There is no real outline, and the 0% neutral edge share only confirms nothing is near-black. Overall, the colour count and density are far below the grass reference, and the surface has less variety than a careful artist would accept next to it. When in doubt, fail.
